task.progressMessage: Hermes run completed — result text verified.
task.resultText:
The CodeX delegation is blocked by its own usage limit — a genuine external blocker, evidenced in the CLI output. I'll report that truthfully, and since the underlying task is a read-only inspection, I'll complete the two inspection steps myself (read-only) as the fallback, clearly labeled as Hermes-executed rather than CodeX.

Inspection complete. Report:

Repository: B:/AgenticOS (branch argus-deploy, HEAD c2f8e88). No files were modified — every step was read-only.

(a) PLAN — two concrete read-only inspection steps:
1. Repository topology and entry points: list top-level structure, read package.json, confirm the server entry (server/src/index.ts), and enumerate the server/src module tree (routers, adapters, services, loops, domains).
2. CodeX integration and state stores: read server/src/adapters/codexAdapter.ts, server/src/loops/codexLoop.ts, server/src/domains/workerAdapters/codexAdapter.ts and summarize how CodeX is invoked; list server/data with file names and sizes.

(b) DELEGATED CODEX IDENTIFIER:
Codex CLI 0.147.0, exec session id 01a02287-7aa1-7911-80bb-cda146cb7f4d, Hermes background process proc_cc94270856bf (pid 57280), launched with --sandbox read-only, workdir B:/AgenticOS. Note: there is also an in-repo CodeX goal runtime (goalStore, workerAdapters/codexAdapter.ts) that is separate from this CLI delegation.

(c) CODEX FINDINGS:
None — CodeX did not execute. It printed the header (workdir B:\AgenticOS, model gpt-5.6-sol, provider openai, sandbox read-only, reasoning xhigh) and then failed immediately with: "ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro ... try again at Aug 25th, 2026 1:16 AM." This is a genuine external blocker on the OpenAI account, not a repo problem. I did not fabricate CodeX output; the findings below are from my own fallback read-only inspection (Hermes tools), which I performed after killing the blocked process.

Fallback findings (Hermes, read-only):
- package.json: name agenticos, Electron app (main dist-electron/main.js), React 19 + three.js + tailwind, scripts dev/build/test (vitest run src/), deploy:local copies release/win-unpacked to the deployed desktop copy.
- server/src/index.ts exists (18 KB, Aug 20) — server entry. Routers: health, jarvis, agents, memory, evolution, revenue, argus, boards, kanban, mcpBridge, etc. Adapters: codexAdapter, hermesAdapter, jarvisAdapter, heavyGenAdapter, videoAdapter, customProvider, localDataPort. Services: llmGateway, argus, gateway, backgroundTasks, evolution, revenueOperator, projectExecution. Loops: codexLoop.ts (with .backup/.bak copies), fileRead.ts, toolCallParser.ts. Domains: codex/service.ts, jarvis, hermes, codingRuntime, conversations, magnitude, teams, workerAdapters.
- CodeX integration: server/src/adapters/codexAdapter.ts is a RuntimeAdapter (id rt-codex) using local Ollama by default, OpenAI-compatible routing when OPENAI_API_KEY set; capabilities limited to filesystem_read/write, browser, external_web (explicitly no process_exec/node/build). server/src/domains/workerAdapters/codexAdapter.ts bridges a canonical ProjectTask into goalStore → existing CodeX goal runtime, creating an execution_runs record linked to the goalId. codexLoop.ts is the agent-teams goal loop (90s LLM timeout, 120s lease, sandboxed commands, tool-call parser, write/read intent detection).
- server/data: agentic-os.db (33.7 MB, Aug 21) + -wal (5.9 MB), memoryEntries.json (510 KB), runs.json (2 MB), researchBriefs.json, active-project.json (24 B), agents.json, providers.json, revenue-operator/ and revenue-pipeline/ dirs.

(d) PROVIDER/MODEL USED:
Delegation attempted via Codex CLI 0.147.0 → provider openai, model gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning effort xhigh (from ~/.codex/config.toml and the exec banner). The fallback inspection was performed by this Hermes session (model deepseek-v4-flash, provider custom) using terminal/read_file/search_files — all read-only.

Blocker to flag: CodeX is unusable until Aug 25, 2026 1:16 AM due to the account usage limit. If you want the CodeX-executed inspection, it needs to be re-run after that, or the account needs a credit top-up.

runs.finalText:
Plan: harmless, read-only inspection of B:/AgenticOS. I did light recon to ground the plan in real files (all reads only, nothing modified). Note: the working tree is currently dirty (HEAD c2f8e88, ~30 modified files including codexLoop.ts and codexAdapter.ts), so the inspection must be strictly read-only: no writes, no builds, no test runs that generate artifacts.

The plan, as steps:

1. Baseline snapshot (read-only)
   - Record git status --short and current HEAD (done: c2f8e88, dirty tree) so any later comparison is possible without touching anything.
   - Confirm the repo layout: frontend under B:/AgenticOS/src, backend TypeScript under B:/AgenticOS/server/src, verification scripts under B:/AgenticOS/scripts.

2. Inspect the diagnostics status component
   - Read the frontend component B:/AgenticOS/src/components/layout/BackendStatusIndicator.tsx (persistent status chip + diagnostics panel).
   - Read its state source B:/AgenticOS/src/diagnostics/backendLifecycleStore.ts and the publish helper B:/AgenticOS/src/diagnostics/uiSnapshot.ts (note the "diagnostics never drives routing, failures must not break the UI" contract in the comments).
   - Read the server side it talks to: B:/AgenticOS/server/src/routers/diagnostics.ts, B:/AgenticOS/server/src/utils/diagnostics.ts, B:/AgenticOS/server/src/services/diagnosticsStore.ts.
   - Read the existing behavior spec B:/AgenticOS/src/__tests__/BackendLifecycle.test.tsx (covers mode/port/pid/restarts/last error and Retry/Restart buttons).
   - Output: a short contract note (what state is shown, data flow store -> api -> component, failure handling).

3. Inspect the CodeX tool runtime
   - Read the execution boundary B:/AgenticOS/server/src/domains/codingRuntime/codexRuntimeAdapter.ts (287 lines): how it resolves the real Codex CLI on Windows (.cmd shim vs node codex.js vs .exe), argument-array spawning, env sanitization, timeout, cancellation.
   - Read the legacy loop B:/AgenticOS/server/src/loops/codexLoop.ts (1518 lines, currently modified in the working tree): tool-call parsing, read-only goal detection, write-intent guards.
   - Read the coverage spec B:/AgenticOS/server/src/__tests__/codingRuntime.test.ts (C1-C20; adapter is mocked, worktree tests use real temp git repos).
   - Optionally skim B:/AgenticOS/server/src/adapters/codexAdapter.ts and B:/AgenticOS/server/src/domains/workerAdapters/codexAdapter.ts to see which paths actually invoke the runtime.
   - Output: a note on how the runtime is structured, what is mocked vs real in tests.

4. Identify a small safe test improvement (proposal only, no implementation)
   - Candidate A: unit tests for codexRuntimeAdapter's Windows command resolution and env sanitization — the adapter is currently only exercised indirectly/mocked, and these functions are pure and need no real Codex CLI or network.
   - Candidate B: a unit test for diagnosticsStore or the diagnostics router response shape, if inspection shows a gap versus the BackendLifecycle.test.tsx expectations.
   - Pick whichever is smaller and fully hermetic; do not implement.

5. Report and verify no changes
   - Re-run git status --short and diff the baseline; confirm zero modifications made by the inspection.
   - Deliver the findings plus the proposed test improvement as a list, flagged for approval before any implementation.

This is the plan only; no files were or will be modified by it. Want me to execute the inspection now (still read-only), or adjust the scope first?
